rationale: Pre-tournament odds make Australia ~1.63 favourites; they are 4-4 with the best NRR, India must win both remaining games, England are 4-4 at home but trail Australia in quality; SA and WI are live outsiders in the shake-up.

Player of Tournament usually goes to a batter on the champion/semi-finalist (2024 Beth Mooney/AUS); Mandhana (159 runs) and Wyatt-Hodge (128 runs) lead the run charts for finalists likely to reach the final, Perry starred for Australia; wicket-takers (Charani, Alleyne) less likely given award convention.

India are reigning T20 World Cup champs and beat England in the 2026 semi-final; England without Carse/Overton and missing several front-liners, but at home with Brook leading and an edge in conditions.

India's July-Zimbabwe squad will be the new T20 set-up (Iyer captain, Abhishek and Samson at the top, Sooryavanshi uncapped); top order most likely to reach 50 first at high-scoring Harare, with seniors rested.

West Indies recalled fit-again Shamar and Alzarri Joseph plus Seales for the Sri Lanka Tests; pace usually dominates at Tarouba, with Shamar's wicket-taking record and Alzarri's home-ground edge making them most likely.

Pakistan were whitewashed 2-0 at home by Bangladesh and are in squad turmoil (seniors dropped), while WI at home in Trinidad with Joseph/Seales/Roach back give an even contest; draw probability high given WI's weak batting and likely rain.

Bangladesh's form batters Shanto, Mushfiqur, Litton (all scored centuries vs Pakistan in May) are the most likely to score a maiden Bangladesh Test ton in Australia; tough Darwin/Mackay conditions for subcontinental batting limit overall likelihood (no century in ~30% of scenarios).

England third Test at Edgbaston in September will likely feature a mixed pace/spin attack (Atkinson, Archer, Tongue, Carse returning, Bashir); most wickets in a single innings tends to fall to front-line quicks, but no clear favourite so spread over top bowlers.

Both Rohit (40 by 2027) and Kohli (39) are expected to make the 2027 World Cup their final one after the 2023 final loss; Rohit's childhood coach says he plans to retire after 2027 WC, making an explicit 'last World Cup' statement most likely.

England are top seed in Pool D and second in the Pro League (26 pts), beating India 4-3 and drawing/short in other games; India have underperformed (near bottom of Pro League) despite a 4-3 win over Pakistan, so England favoured.

ECB confirmed in March 2026 that McCullum continues as head coach across all formats and is contracted to the end of the 2027 ODI World Cup, so an appointment of a permanent successor by July 29 is unlikely; alternatives only if England's New Zealand Test series result forces a change.
